Why are there so many negative reviews?
Yes, this is Diablo with a nice coat of paint, but the paint is VERY pretty! It's snacky, it's flashy, it's filled with quality of life improvements. It's all here from Diablo and similar games too: side quests, collectable dyes and skins, treasure goblins (called Omen of Wealth), socketed items, the Path of Exile like wheel of minor improvements leading to larger improvements, skills that level up through use, bosses, allies, shrines, tiers...all present and accounted for. But the enemies tend towards the strange over the generic and so do the locations: glittering palaces of opulence, battlefields overlooked by steampunk cannons, shipwreck graveyards. The dialogue is snarky but not too annoying, and easy to ignore since it tends to happen mid-battle. I didn't encounter any glitches. 
This is a slower and deliberate game than a lot of loot hack/slash types, but I liked the impact, the physics mixed with satisfying death animations. I guess a problem would be the online component is dead, but the single player seems smooth and fun still!
If you want Diablo mixed with a little Torchlight (pets collect loot) and Path of Exile, check it out!

Developer got their bag then abandoned their game. 
All multiplayer was online and had to go through the developer's servers, and then they killed it without adding the ability to host our own lobbies, so it's permanently single player only. 
WOLCEN Studio is now attempting to develop an online-only, live service game.  DO NOT give this company your money!

Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem—a name so full of promise, you’d think it was forged in the fires of Mount Doom and polished with the tears of underpaid indie developers. But no! What we got was a glittering skeleton wrapped in tinfoil and duct tape, doomed to crumble before it ever stood tall. NYEHHH!

The first few hours? Glorious! The graphics? Stunning! You stroll into battle wielding lightning, shadows, and the hopes of everyone who thought "Finally, a true Diablo killer!" But then… reality bites. And it bites hard.

Let’s talk about the gameplay—because oh dear, sweet necrotic failure, it wants to be something. The combat is flashy, the skill system is cool in theory, and the classless freedom? Delightful… until you realize that balance was left in the developer’s sock drawer during early access and never retrieved.

And the bugs, oh the bugs! This game launched like it was trying to speedrun its own obituary. Crashes, desyncs, invisible enemies, disappearing loot—it was like fighting both demons and the spaghetti code they rode in on. You didn’t die in Wolcen because you made mistakes—you died because the server sneezed.

Ah yes, the servers. R.I.P. You will not be missed. Multiplayer was a catastrophe from day one. You had a better chance of summoning an actual demon than getting a stable co-op session. And now? Shut down. Gone. Vanished into the void. Like the developers’ long-term roadmap. All that’s left is offline mode and the echoes of what could have been.

And let’s not forget: they pulled the plug quietly, like rats leaving a sinking ship. No big send-off. Just a whisper: “No sequel. No more updates. Good luck with your necromancer, loser.” Bravo. Truly, a masterclass in vanishing before the pitchforks arrive.

Final Verdict: 💀💀⬛⬛⬛ (2 out of 5 Skulls)

ARPG Wolcen is actually quite alright and far from a disappointment. Then again I don't have any history with it, so I'm likely more inclined to forgive its missteps. 

I struggle to call out something that is unique to Wolcen, besides the gorgeous graphics and the incredible soundtrack. And the game takes the time to tell its story through dialogue and (quite decent) cutscenes. Enemies are well animated and some look very imposing. Animations actually take priority above snappiness, so it makes running and dodging for example feel a little bit more heavy/sluggish (but IMO not in a bad way). There's some physics involved as well, so you'll see bodies slowly fall down stairs. Nice detail. Wolcen's not a very loot heavy game, at least not as much as for example Diablo 3. Item pre- and suffices are simplified as well, especially compared to Grim Dawn. The skill system is very intuitive, with all kinds of modifiers enhancing the baseline skill. The use of skills and magic is balanced with a meter. The more magic you use (wisdom), the less rage you have (skills need rage) and vice versa. 

Wolcen isn't always the best in explaining its mechanics and numbers. Some skill upgrades blatently state "the upgrade will do more damage", but how much is that? Some of the explanations are very clear and others are very vague. It's very inconsistent. About the bugs: besides some items laying on the ground not being labeled and two hard crashes (in almost 42 hours playtime) everything worked fine.

All things considered I'd say Wolcen is a very casual friendly ARPG and a game I would recommend to someone new to the genre. And certainly when you can get it at a discount. I'm not the kind of gamer that keeps replaying the same content, so after 42 hours I was done with it. But as a total package it was an enjoyable experience.

Rating: 7.0/10

you’re an ARPG collector

you’re okay knowing this game isn’t going anywhere
you get it a DEEP discount

Item pre- and suffices are simplified as well, especially compared to Grim Dawn. The skill system is very intuitive, with all kinds of modifiers enhancing the baseline skill. The use of skills and magic is balanced with a meter. The more magic you use (wisdom), the less rage you have (skills need rage) and vice versa. 

Wolcen isn't always the best in explaining its mechanics and numbers. Some skill upgrades blatently state "the upgrade will do more damage", but how much is that? Some of the explanations are very clear and others are very vague. It's very inconsistent. About the bugs: besides some items laying on the ground not being labeled and two hard crashes (in almost 42 hours playtime) everything worked fine.

All things considered I'd say Wolcen is a very casual friendly ARPG and a game I would recommend to someone new to the genre. And certainly when you can get it at a discount. I'm not the kind of gamer that keeps replaying the same content, so after 42 hours I was done with it. But as a total package it was an enjoyable experience.

Pretty game with some really ambitious ideas. It's a shame they jumped the shark with a 1.0 release and most of those ideas just didn't function. I remember getting it in early access back when you could still rotate the camera and the starting experience was much different. It did still have the dual resource system that the current game has, which is one of the ideas I thought was really cool. You'd mouse over them, they'd have a tooltip, you could invest a point, but then they simply didn't do anything. Very frustrating to find out. I never planned on posting a review on this game.....the player count on release was encouraging and I even gifted this one to a few friends. 

That said:

This is not not a game that will get any better as the Dev team has abandoned it. If in doubt, just Google it and watch a build guide or new player breakdown - you will know in a few minutes if this is what you're looking for to scratch the ARPG itch.

Where to start?....its a great single player ARPG. That said, if you're looking for something more than fun single player ARPG that delivers seasons and multiplayer, this ain't it. 

If you like isometric ARPGs in single player, this game is a ton of fun. The campaign is great and the single player side is addicting. The story *mode* and the visuals are amazing. & combat is fluid...those do so much to carry a dead game.  They did nail the engine though and combat....even low spec PCs are going to be surprised. 

Once you get the endgame, it just sort of falls off....not all at once, but over time. Building a city is boring at best, and straight up tedious at worst; there is NOT a payoff for progression at this point.

Its a fun game for the ARPG fiends...truly. Beyond that, its just not for anyone expecting a Diablo of PoE experience; what you see is what you get.

There is currently a sale for $1.99 so I decided to review it: if you love the game genre, $1.99 is a freaking steal; it absolutely worth two bucks.

My advice: its two dollars and that should be your guiding star if this is your genre......this is definitely worth more than an McDonalds kids meal. Again, if you need more info, just Google it.....definitely worth the cost of entry at this point....just make sure you snag it on sale.

Se você está considerando adquirir Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem, é fundamental entender que você não está comprando um jogo vivo, mas sim um projeto que foi formalmente abandonado por seus criadores. O que outrora prometeu ser um competidor de peso no mercado de ARPGs, hoje é pouco mais do que uma relíquia de um desenvolvimento conturbado.

O Fim do Suporte: Uma Traição aos Jogadores
O maior pecado de Wolcen não é o design, mas a postura do estúdio. Após anos de uma comunicação errática, falhas técnicas constantes e a promessa de uma narrativa maior, o Wolcen Studio simplesmente "jogou a toalha".

Abandono Total: Desde setembro de 2024, o jogo não conta mais com servidores multiplayer. O suporte ao desenvolvimento foi encerrado permanentemente.

Narrativa Incompleta: O jogo foi vendido sob a premissa de uma história épica de cinco atos. O suporte foi cortado após o quarto ato, deixando os jogadores que investiram no título com uma trama inacabada e sem qualquer perspectiva de conclusão.

Legado de Incompetência: A decisão de encerrar as operações foi justificada pela empresa como uma limitação tecnológica do motor do jogo, que os impedia de corrigir problemas estruturais persistentes. Isso levanta uma questão óbvia: por que lançar e cobrar por um produto construído sobre uma base técnica que eles sabiam ser insustentável?

Problemas Persistentes
Mesmo jogando no modo offline, a experiência de Wolcen é marcada por cicatrizes de um ciclo de vida mal gerido:

Bugs de "Early Access": Apesar de estar fora do acesso antecipado há anos, o jogo ainda sofre com bugs de colisão, problemas de performance em áreas densas e falhas que podem travar o progresso em missões.

Falta de Polimento: A interface (UI) e a experiência do usuário (UX) parecem datadas e frequentemente desajeitadas, tornando a gestão de inventário e a navegação pelos menus um processo frustrante quando comparado aos padrões atuais da indústria.

With the hype they received and all the copies sold they did really disappoint in what they delivered after the release and now just abandoning the whole game, removing features which were working before (online-mode) is a no-go.

I thought this game would go somewhere but it felt like the devs did a quick money grab... rarely updated and then decided to cease online/multiplayer support and abandon the game for other money grab projects. I will not be supporting any of their other projects going forward. Do so with caution.

Wolcen is a fairly divisive Diablo-style ARPG with some interesting ideas with mixed implementation but having a few highlights as well. From my understanding, Wolcen was very heavily changed from original Kickstarter plans which annoyed backers. Then released most of the game after ending Early Access leading to a really rough and buggy launch. I picked it up on discount years after it's release, a number of minor bugs here and there and a few crashes but nothing totally game breaking in offline mode and the campaign has been 'finished'.

Wolcen is currently getting a lot of hate due to announcing on May 30th 2024 that they are ceasing further development and support for the game and closing the multiplayer servers on September 3, 2024. It was already pretty obvious that the devs were finished updating game, losing multiplayer is a bigger issue. I assume they choose to do this because Wolcen player pop is pretty low. Unfortunately, like many other modern games, there is no alternate local multi-player supported so once the servers are closed multiplayer functionality will cease. The Community Manager reported that the devs are planning to release a "Import Online Character" button to download and convert your online character to an offline one, even when the server is already shut down so at least there's that.


Pros:
* Has one of the better campaigns in the genre I'd say. A bit cliche at times but well done with decent cutscenes, voice acting, good character designs and a few interesting characters. The final fourth chapter was released post-release and is weaker than original (no waypoints, it's more of a rougue-lite type experience with a couple of story missions and a lot of grinding to be able to fight the final boss Ahriman) but still overall worth finishing off the campaign.
* Graphics are overall pretty good.

Se você está considerando adquirir Wolcen: Lords of Mayhem, é fundamental entender que você não está comprando um jogo vivo, mas sim um projeto que foi formalmente abandonado por seus criadores. O que outrora prometeu ser um competidor de peso no mercado de ARPGs, hoje é pouco mais do que uma relíquia de um desenvolvimento conturbado.

O Fim do Suporte: Uma Traição aos Jogadores
O maior pecado de Wolcen não é o design, mas a postura do estúdio. Após anos de uma comunicação errática, falhas técnicas constantes e a promessa de uma narrativa maior, o Wolcen Studio simplesmente "jogou a toalha".

Abandono Total: Desde setembro de 2024, o jogo não conta mais com servidores multiplayer. O suporte ao desenvolvimento foi encerrado permanentemente.

Narrativa Incompleta: O jogo foi vendido sob a premissa de uma história épica de cinco atos. O suporte foi cortado após o quarto ato, deixando os jogadores que investiram no título com uma trama inacabada e sem qualquer perspectiva de conclusão.

Legado de Incompetência: A decisão de encerrar as operações foi justificada pela empresa como uma limitação tecnológica do motor do jogo, que os impedia de corrigir problemas estruturais persistentes. Isso levanta uma questão óbvia: por que lançar e cobrar por um produto construído sobre uma base técnica que eles sabiam ser insustentável?

Problemas Persistentes
Mesmo jogando no modo offline, a experiência de Wolcen é marcada por cicatrizes de um ciclo de vida mal gerido:

Bugs de "Early Access": Apesar de estar fora do acesso antecipado há anos, o jogo ainda sofre com bugs de colisão, problemas de performance em áreas densas e falhas que podem travar o progresso em missões.

Falta de Polimento: A interface (UI) e a experiência do usuário (UX) parecem datadas e frequentemente desajeitadas, tornando a gestão de inventário e a navegação pelos menus um processo frustrante quando comparado aos padrões atuais da indústria.
